# git: alias: keep commit dates monotonic in at/contrib and on squash

Make the date-setting commit aliases refuse to go back in time, and give squashing a way to keep dates. **Motivation:** a linear history should have monotonic dates. `git at` and `git contrib` put one timestamp into both author and committer dates without looking at the parent, so a suggested or typed time earlier than `HEAD` silently produces a child older than its parent (seen in the wild: two same-day commits in reversed order, author = committer on both). Separately, `rebase -i` squash/fixup resets the committer date to now, leaving a lone commit hours or months "ahead" of its neighbours; `git amend` ([[DOT-352]]) and `git rewrite` ([[DOT-498]]) already preserve dates, squashing has no such path.

PoC of the defect:

```bash
$ git commit --allow-empty -m parent                  # committed now
$ git at '-1 hour' child                              # accepted today
$ git log -2 --format='%h %ct %s'                     # child %ct < parent %ct
```

Expected interface:

```bash
$ git at '-1 hour' child
git-at: 2026-09-23T10:00:00+03:00 is earlier than HEAD (2026-09-23T11:00:00+03:00)
$ echo $?                                             # non-zero, nothing committed
```

1. `git at`, `git contrib`: compare the timestamp with `git log -1 --format=%ct` (and `%at`) of `HEAD`; if earlier, print an error to stderr and return non-zero. No `HEAD` (first commit) — no check.
2. Squash preserving dates: a rebase entry point (e.g. `rebase -i --committer-date-is-author-date`, merge backend) so squashed/fixup commits keep their author date as the committer date. Overlaps with the fixup alias in [[DOT-343]] — decide there or here, not twice.

Out of scope: rewriting existing histories, `git it` (no parent), `pull --rebase` in the sync scripts.
